item.title: Mexico is phasing in a higher cruise passenger tax, and for travel agents the first thing to get right is a UK compliance point.
item.description:
Mexico is phasing in a higher cruise passenger tax, and for travel agents the first thing to get right is a UK compliance point.
One: under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024, this mandatory charge must show up front in the price a client sees, so pricing systems should reflect it from the start. Two: the fee doubled to £7.40 per person on 1 August 2026, rises to £11.10 in July 2027, and reaches £14.80 by August 2028. Three: it applies once per itinerary, not per port call, so the real cost stays modest, roughly £30 for a couple by 2028.

item.title: easyJet holidays has launched a £100-per-booking discount for travel agents, and here are the three points to know.
item.description:
easyJet holidays has launched a £100-per-booking discount for travel agents, and here are the three points to know.
One, it is trade-only. Agents quote the code TRADEEXCLUSIVE on a minimum spend of £1,000 per booking, and clients booking direct cannot access it.
Two, the timing. New bookings must be made before 11pm on 1 September 2026, for holidays departing between 19 August 2026 and 31 October 2027.
Three, the range. It covers beach and city packages across Europe and North Africa, with the Luxury Collection included. easyJet holidays says the offer marks six years of working with the trade.

item.title: Small-ship cruising is drawing a fresh crowd of guests. Demand is coming from first-time cruisers: Unforgettable Croatia reports 68% of its summer bookings are new to cruise, many from a boutique-hotel background. The scale is a big part of the draw, with small-ship lines such as Windstar, Ponant and HX Expeditions carrying fewer than 600 guests, and Windstar between 148 and 342. Food does plenty of the selling too, as 60% of sailors name food and drink as the best part of a cruise, and Windstar gives its chef a generous local-market budget on port days.

item.title: New Barclays Consumer Card Spending data, reported by Cruise Trade News, is worth sitting with this week.
item.description:
New Barclays Consumer Card Spending data, reported by Cruise Trade News, is worth sitting with this week.
One, travel agent spend grew again in July, up 2.5% year on year, the second consecutive month of growth.
Two, that came even as overall travel spend slipped 0.3% and airline spend fell 6.0% over the same month, while hotels and accommodation rose 2.6%.
Three, the wider backdrop held firm, with UK card spending up 2.0% in July and reaching its highest level in 12 months.
Taken together, clients are booking with care rather than booking less, and still choosing to book through agents.

item.title: The Rhône is one of the strongest rivers to sell right now. Tauck reports its Rhône bookings pacing nearly 30 percent ahead of 2025, before the line's expansion has begun.
item.description:
The Rhône is one of the strongest rivers to sell right now. Tauck reports its Rhône bookings pacing nearly 30 percent ahead of 2025, before the line's expansion has begun.
To meet the demand, Tauck has announced a new vessel, MS Harmonie. A sister ship to MS Lumière, she carries a maximum of 130 guests, up to 30 percent fewer than comparable riverboats. She launches in 2028.
She's part of a bigger build: five new riverboats between 2026 and 2028, growing Tauck's river capacity by more than 50 percent, with expanded shoulder-season departures and new six-day formats. For agents, that's strong demand to sell now, and a fresh ship to flag for clients planning ahead.

item.title: Three points worth knowing if you book European travel for clients.
item.description:
Three points worth knowing if you book European travel for clients.
One, the EU's new Entry/Exit System, the biometric border scheme known as EES, went fully live in April 2026, and airports have warned of queues up to three hours at peak, some hubs approaching five.
Two, the Independent reports the EU could delay further post-Brexit border measures to keep this summer moving.
Three, Schengen countries can partly suspend the checks for up to 90 days to ease congestion, and any suspension is applied country by country, not EU-wide.
The picture, then, depends on where your client is flying into, which is exactly the context worth having ready when the worried questions arrive.

item.title: easyJet is set to change hands, and here are three points worth knowing.
item.description:

item.title: Princess Cruises has shared its agent selling tips on the Cruise Corner podcast, and there are three worth noting.
item.description:
Princess Cruises has shared its agent selling tips on the Cruise Corner podcast, and there are three worth noting.
One, and the most practical in a booking conversation, match the ship to the traveller. The line runs a range of ship sizes, so there is a fit for couples and families alike.
Two, treat the partnerships with global brands as a selling point in their own right.
Three, sell the whole value, both the onboard amenities and the shoreside experiences, which widens the appeal across ages.
UK sales director Yasmin McKechnie also suggests positioning a cruise as a once in a lifetime experience for clients.

Fresh cruise search data from World of Cruising, reported by Cruise Trade News, is worth a look this morning.
Three things to know:
1. The Mediterranean is up around 44% year on year and now accounts for nearly half of all cruise searches, against 33% a year ago.
2. Caribbean demand has fallen about 27%, while wider European sailings hold steady at roughly 30% of searches.
3. Clients are booking closer to departure, with 52% of exact-month searches now for trips within 16 weeks, up from 45%.
The takeaway from Cruise Trade News's Raphael Giacardi: focus on summer and autumn 2026 short-haul, and remember these markets can move quickly.

item.title: Wildfires on Crete have forced evacuations affecting around 8,000 residents and tourists, and as of 31 July 2026 the situation is still developing. Three things worth knowing for anyone with clients on the island.
item.description:
Wildfires on Crete have forced evacuations affecting around 8,000 residents and tourists, and as of 31 July 2026 the situation is still developing. Three things worth knowing for anyone with clients on the island.
One, the UK advice is to stay in touch with your travel provider, follow local safety instructions, and avoid cancelling prematurely.
Two, Which? Travel's Rory Boland warns that "travellers who cancel now will likely forfeit the right to a refund or rebooking." A rushed cancellation can remove a client's protection.
Three, for a booked client, their agent is that provider. The steadying role of watching official advice and protecting the booking sits with you.

item.title: New data from 247 Travel Partner Desk (247tpd), a travel-only support provider, is a timely reminder as heatwaves disrupt journeys across Europe.
item.description:
New data from 247 Travel Partner Desk (247tpd), a travel-only support provider, is a timely reminder as heatwaves disrupt journeys across Europe.
Three things worth knowing:
1. Specialist human support reached resolution quality of up to 90%, and 100% in some cases. 2. AI-only support scored 69%, roughly a 30% gap in favour of people. 3. The figures are 247tpd's own, from a business focused entirely on travel disruption.
The read is simple. When trips get complicated, experienced people resolve things more reliably than software alone. For clients heading into the heat, that means checking flexibility before departure and knowing who to call if disruption hits, not waiting in an app queue.

item.title: A useful read for anyone planning winter flights.
item.description:
A useful read for anyone planning winter flights.
Aviation analyst John Strickland of JLS Consulting has forecast that European and US airlines could ground more aircraft than usual this winter as high fuel costs bite. He shared it at a World Aviation Festival webinar on 16 July 2026. It's a professional forecast, not a confirmed schedule change.
The part worth acting on is the split. The marginal routes, quieter city pairs and thin, off-peak services, are where capacity could tighten first. The busy winter-sun corridors are barely exposed. So the clients worth an early word are those booked on the thinner routes, where booking early protects choice on price and timings.

item.title: Cunard has opened a 10% loyalty saving for returning guests, and a few points are worth noting for the trade.
item.description:
Cunard has opened a 10% loyalty saving for returning guests, and a few points are worth noting for the trade.
Start with the timing. Bookings qualify from 23 July to 31 August 2026, on eligible Cunard Fare or Early Saver Fare voyages of 7 to 67 nights departing between January 2027 and March 2028.
The scale matters too. In 2027, three Queens ships return to UK roundtrip sailings for the first time since 2018, lifting Southampton capacity by 54 percent.
And whichever itinerary a guest chooses, Cunard's White Star service is included on every voyage.

item.title: Around 2.2 million British holidaymakers travel abroad this bank-holiday weekend, and EES is now part of the border picture.
item.description:
Around 2.2 million British holidaymakers travel abroad this bank-holiday weekend, and EES is now part of the border picture. Three things worth knowing:
1. EES has been in full force since April. Non-EU travellers register, are photographed, and give fingerprints on arrival, which can slow passport control at busier crossings.
2. ABTA expects Spain to lead demand this weekend, with Greece, Portugal, Italy and Turkey close behind.
3. Greece has indicated it won't apply the additional biometric checks for UK nationals.
For agents, the value is timing and reassurance. A clear pre-departure note keeps clients calm.

item.title: New UK research is worth a read for anyone selling holidays this summer. Three things stood out.
item.description:
New UK research is worth a read for anyone selling holidays this summer. Three things stood out.
People are protecting the holiday above almost everything else, with 65% happy to skip dining out, hobbies and cinema trips before they touch the trip fund. They want it bundled too, with half asking for one price that covers accommodation, meals and entertainment. And they are not sitting on their hands: 51% now let destination affordability lead the booking, and 75% are booking now rather than waiting.
For agents, this is a value story, not a discount one. When clients want everything accounted for in a single number, that is a professional's job, not a search engine's.

item.description:

item.title: Three practical things worth knowing before clients fly home from Europe this summer.
item.description:
Three practical things worth knowing before clients fly home from Europe this summer.
One: the EU's new entry-exit system, the EES, has nearly tripled passport-control times for Brits at some airports, with Rome's Fiumicino reporting a rise from 7 minutes to 20.
Two: Wizz Air UK now advises UK passengers to arrive three hours before the flight home, up from two, and to bring a portable charger and water for the queue.
Three: it varies by country. France reports no major congestion at its hubs, and biometric e-gate kiosks are helping ease the busiest points.
A short heads-up before clients travel makes the difference.

item.title: Three things worth knowing from the latest Barclays Consumer Spend research.
item.description:
Three things worth knowing from the latest Barclays Consumer Spend research.
One: spending with UK travel agents grew 1.9% in June, ending three months of decline after falls of 5.7% in April and 5.8% in May.
Two: overall travel spending was flat at down 0.1%, with airline spend down 5.4% while hotels and accommodation rose 1.7%.
Three: 26% of UK consumers now plan a staycation this year, up from 19% in April.
A steadying picture for the agent channel, and a useful read on where clients are placing their trust.

item.title: With the 2026 heatwave across Europe and North Africa, plenty of clients are heading somewhere hot this summer. The Independent published useful heat advice from Tamara Davison, a British writer living in Dahab, Egypt. Three things worth passing on.
item.description:
With the 2026 heatwave across Europe and North Africa, plenty of clients are heading somewhere hot this summer. The Independent published useful heat advice from Tamara Davison, a British writer living in Dahab, Egypt. Three things worth passing on.
One, pace beats hustle. Early starts, slower middays, siestas welcomed rather than fought.
Two, hydration has nuance. Room-temperature drinks over ice-cold, electrolyte sachets from any pharmacy, frozen grapes as a snack.
Three, air conditioning has a downside. It can dry out sinuses, so a little added humidity helps.
A short pre-departure note turns all of that into a client who feels looked after.

item.title: Crystal Cruises' Luke Smith, VP of UK and EMEA Sales, shared a practical steer for agents selling ultra-luxury. Three things worth knowing.
item.description:
Crystal Cruises' Luke Smith, VP of UK and EMEA Sales, shared a practical steer for agents selling ultra-luxury. Three things worth knowing.
1. Sell the total value, not the headline fare. Compare the price your clients pay to get off the ship, once gratuities, Wi-Fi and beverages are counted, and ultra-luxury looks far more competitive.
2. Product knowledge counts. Understanding the nuances between Crystal, Seabourn, Silversea and Regent Seven Seas helps you match clients to the right line.
3. Look after loyal cruisers. A milestone birthday or anniversary is often the moment a repeat client is ready to upgrade.

item.title: Three things to know on the EU's Entry/Exit System (EES) this week.
item.description:
Three things to know on the EU's Entry/Exit System (EES) this week.
1. Ryanair has named seven airports where EES is causing the worst queues: Tenerife South, Palma, Alicante, Malaga, Milan Bergamo, Krakow and Paris Beauvais. Passengers on Schengen routes are being advised to arrive earlier than usual.
2. Port of Dover declared a critical incident during May half-term, with waits of up to 4.5 hours. CEO Doug Bannister has warned of severe congestion through peak weeks, when volumes are expected to exceed 12,000 vehicles a day.
3. Greece has already suspended its EES rollout, and Ryanair is calling for a broader pause until September.

item.title: Travel Weekly is reporting a potential price "bloodbath" predicted in late summer.
item.description:
Travel Weekly is reporting a potential price "bloodbath" predicted in late summer. For agents, that single line is the most useful piece of market intelligence this week, and there are three reasons it matters this week.
First, the late-booking window is already active. UK agents are reporting late bookings building well into July, so a back-half price story doesn't slow demand, it sharpens it.
Second, it gives every agent a clean, honest line for the hesitating client. If a client is weighing up a late-summer booking, you can flag the Travel Weekly read, offer to hold an option for a week if they're flexible, and explain why locking in now is the safer play if they're not.
Third, it puts the agent ahead of the headline. By Friday at least one client will have seen the story in their feed. The agents who've already read the original report are the ones who sound confident when the phone rings.

item.title: The UK's FCDO lifted its Gulf travel advisory on 18 June, covering the UAE, Qatar and Saudi Arabia. Australia moved the same day.
item.description:
The UK's FCDO lifted its Gulf travel advisory on 18 June, covering the UAE, Qatar and Saudi Arabia. Australia moved the same day.
Three things worth knowing for the trade right now:
1. UK carriers and operators are flying Gulf routes. Bookings to Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Doha, Riyadh and Jeddah can be confirmed against UK government guidance today.
2. EASA has not yet cleared Gulf airspace for European Union carriers. Lufthansa, Air France and KLM remain grounded on those routes, with clearance expected around October 2026.
3. UK agents currently hold a connectivity advantage their European counterparts do not. The FCDO page remains the live source of truth, and operator risk assessments should be checked alongside.

item.title: Qantas has confirmed Sydney to London as the first Project Sunrise route, launching October 2027.
item.description:
Qantas has confirmed Sydney to London as the first Project Sunrise route, launching October 2027.
Three things worth knowing for the trade:
1. It's the first non-stop between Australia's east coast and the UK, ending nearly 80 years of stopovers on the Kangaroo Route and saving up to four hours versus current journey times.
2. The aircraft is a custom Airbus A350-1000ULR with an additional 20,000-litre fuel tank for the 22-hour flight. 12 ordered, 238 seats across four cabins.
3. Tickets are expected on sale February 2027. Existing Perth-London and Sydney-Singapore-London services continue, and Sydney-New York is confirmed as the next Sunrise route.

item.title: Consumer confidence in travel is up. The booking window has narrowed.
item.description:
Travel Weekly's exclusive consumer tracking data shows UK confidence in booking an overseas summer holiday has rallied significantly since late April 2026. The booking window, however, has narrowed.
Three things worth noting for agents this fortnight:
1. Intent is up. The proportion of people planning to travel in the next three months has risen.
2. Conversion is lagging. Clients are planning to travel soon and leaving the booking itself until later.
3. The opportunity sits in the gap. Confidence is the harder problem to solve, and that part has already moved. The nudge between intention and confirmation is where a named agent earns the booking.
